connectionPanel.chargesOnBoot: This ArduPilot only charges on boot: press Respawn
connectionPanel.clientHint: Connect to a remote device at this address
connectionPanel.crsfHint: The telemetry an ExpressLRS transmitter broadcasts over WiFi. Set Telemetry Mode to WiFi in the ELRS Lua script and join the backpack network, then listen here on port 14550. Works behind any CRSF receiver, INAV included, with nothing changed on the aircraft.
connectionPanel.crsfReadOnly: Read-only: position, attitude, altitude, battery, flight mode and link quality. No missions, parameters, mode changes or commands, because the link only goes one way.
connectionPanel.crsfTitle: CRSF telemetry from an ExpressLRS backpack
connectionPanel.crsfTwoWay: For a two-way link, switch the ELRS Link Mode to MAVLink and connect with the MAVLink option instead. That needs an ESP-based transmitter on ELRS 3.5 or newer (backpack 1.5+), a fast packet rate, and INAV 8+ with the receiver UART set to MAVLink at 460800 (Receiver: SERIAL, protocol MAVLINK). INAV is still configured over USB either way.
connectionPanel.driverHelp: Device not showing? Get driver help
connectionPanel.elrsWizardHint: Guided setup - finds and configures it for you
connectionPanel.elrsWizardTip: Guided setup for an ExpressLRS module as your telemetry radio
connectionPanel.forwardHint: Mirrors this link's raw MAVLink to other devices over UDP and relays their commands back. Any UDP peer that can reach this port is picked up automatically once it sends a heartbeat - a phone on the same WiFi, or one with no network at all, bridged in over USB - or enter its address below.
connectionPanel.listenHint: Listen for incoming packets on this port
connectionPanel.localPortHint: Source port for outgoing packets. Keep stable across reconnects: ArduPilot caches the first source endpoint it sees and replies there for the rest of the link. Change only if 14550 is in use locally.
connectionPanel.openRadioSetup: Open Radio Setup - it fixes this for you
connectionPanel.px4DownloadFailed: Failed to download PX4 SITL bundle.
connectionPanel.px4DownloadFailedDetail: Failed to download PX4 SITL bundle: {{detail}}
connectionPanel.respawnTip: Reboot the simulated vehicle: back on the ground at home, disarmed
connectionPanel.signingHint: Accepts passphrases, base64 keys (from Mission Planner), or hex keys. All keys are tried automatically on connect.
connectionPanel.sitlAutoConnectFailed: Could not connect to SITL. Try connecting manually.
connectionPanel.sitlConnectFailed: Could not connect to SITL. Make sure it is running on TCP port 5760.
connectionPanel.sitlProcessFailed: SITL process failed to start. Check the SITL tab for details.
connectionPanel.startedOutside: Started outside ArduDeck: Stop only ends simulators this app launched.

multiVehicle.cellularHint: The drone dials in to this machine. Point its telemetry forwarder ({{forwarder}}) at this machine's reachable address on port {{port}}. The link recovers on its own across signal loss and carrier NAT changes.
multiVehicle.listeningEmpty: Listening. Vehicles appear here the moment their heartbeats arrive.
multiVehicle.startHint: Finds your vehicles automatically. No setup.
multiVehicle.tcpHint: ArduDeck dials the drone's address. Use this when the drone has a reachable IP.

orchestration.noSelection: No vehicles selected; server decides scope
orchestration.title: Orchestration

radioSetup.checkingVehicle: Connected. Checking the vehicle for radio-link readiness...
radioSetup.doneHint: Telemetry, stick control and signal strength all flow through the radio. The SiK-style modem workflow applies from here: just connect on {{radio}} whenever you fly or drive.
radioSetup.elrs400Warning: This module runs ELRS 4.0.0, which corrupts stick positions in MAVLink mode. Update it (and the receiver) to 4.0.1 or newer before operating with sticks.
radioSetup.listeningWifi: Listening for a WiFi radio (TX Backpack)...
radioSetup.needsSwitch: The radio needs to switch to MAVLink mode to carry telemetry.
radioSetup.noRadio: No radio found - two ways to hook one up:
radioSetup.noUsbDevices: No USB serial devices were present.
radioSetup.portOpenFailed: Could not open the port. Is another program using it?
radioSetup.powerBackOn: Power the vehicle back on and give the link a few seconds to come up, then connect.
radioSetup.powerOffHint: The radio refuses this change while its receiver is linked. Unpower the vehicle completely - battery out AND USB cable unplugged. You can also press Start now and unpower the vehicle while ArduDeck keeps retrying.
radioSetup.radioReady: The radio on {{radio}} is ready and speaking MAVLink.
radioSetup.readingSettings: Reading vehicle settings over the radio...
radioSetup.restartRejected: The restart command was not accepted.
radioSetup.restartingVehicle: Restarting the vehicle - the link reconnects by itself...
radioSetup.stillReports: Module still reports {{mode}} - waiting for the receiver to go dark.
radioSetup.switchTimeout: The module kept refusing the change - the receiver was still powered and linked. Unpower the vehicle completely (battery AND USB cable) and press Start again.
radioSetup.title: Radio Setup
radioSetup.usbHint: Plug the radio module into this computer with a USB data cable. It can stay in the handset bay - it just also needs the cable to this computer.
radioSetup.wifiHint: Radios built into the handset (e.g. TX16S internal) have no USB - they stream over WiFi instead. Enable Backpack WiFi from the ELRS menu on the handset, then either join this computer to the "ExpressLRS TX Backpack" network (password: expresslrs) or put the backpack on your home WiFi. Note: WiFi streaming only works once the radio link is already in MAVLink mode - switching the mode itself needs USB or the handset menu.
radioSetup.wifiListenFailed: Could not listen on the WiFi port. Is another program using UDP 14550?
radioSetup.wifiTitle: WiFi (TX Backpack - required for internal modules)
